# Wolfpack

> Wolfpack is a self-hosted control room for persistent coding-agent terminals on your own machines.

## What it does
- Runs beside coding agents on macOS or Linux and serves a browser/PWA dashboard for laptop, workstation and phone.
- Shows which agent needs you: sessions waiting for input are pinned in a "Needs you" band and sorted first; filters narrow the list to Needs you, Working, Idle or Failed.
- Answers from anywhere: on desktop a needs-input banner sends y, n or Esc in one click; on a phone the live terminal and its keyboard accessory are the reply surface.
- Keeps every session alive: a local Rust PTY broker owns the terminals, so agents survive closed tabs, dropped connections and web-server restarts.
- Lists sessions from every verified machine on a Tailscale tailnet, grouped by machine.
- Lets agents run agents: a CLI to create sessions, spawn child agents that notify their parent, send input, wait for output and follow events, locally or with `--machine` on another machine.
- Built-in coding-agent provider choices: Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI, Cursor, Pi.
- Shell is the always-available fallback. Custom commands and wrappers on PATH are supported separately.

## Privacy and architecture
- Open source under the MIT license.
- No Wolfpack account is required.
- No Wolfpack-hosted relay or prompt-upload service is used; remote access normally travels over the operator's Tailscale network.
- Sessions are owned by a local Rust PTY broker and survive web-server restarts.
